thread:
alex: Heads up — noticed a weird billing spike in ap-southeast1 for the inference fleet. Monthly GPU+egress cost is ~42% above our forecast for Feb. Exported the rough CSV, putting the snippet below. Can someone eyeball?

priya: Thanks alex. Can you drop the export link? I can run the cost breakdown query and map by sku.

alex: link: https://internal.redwood/billing/exports/1873456789.csv (accessible to infra + finance)

alex: CSV snip:
```
region,resource,usage_hours,cost_usd
ap-southeast1,a2-highgpu-1g,6480,46200.12
ap-southeast1,n2-standard-8,720,3120.00
us-west1,a2-highgpu-1g,4320,24150.75
us-central1,a2-highgpu-1g,1200,6900.30

network_egress_apac,TB,12.4,12400.00
```

jordan: oof. Egress is the big one here (12.4TB). Any changes in model placement or cross-region replication last month?

elena: We had a short test in late Jan to replicate embeddings cache from ap-southeast1 -> us-central1 for DR. That would explain cross-region egress. Who kicked that off?

priya: that was my test. I forgot to tear down the background sync for 2 weeks — my bad. But still want to see if commitments/reserved capacity could have lowered unit costs even with the extra egress.

tyler: From finance perspective, two things: (1) committed use discount heels are significant in APAC on the a2 SKU if we lock 1yr (estimate ~22% off), (2) egress is charged separately and won't be reduced by committing compute. We should differentiate compute vs network tradeoffs.

alex: Agree. Quick back-of-envelope: if we commit 50% baseline in ap-southeast1 for 1yr at 22% savings, we save ~ (46200 * 0.5 * 0.22) ~= $5082/mo vs current. But egress still ~12k extra one-off.

jordan: Also consider spot/interruptible for batch workloads — those contributed ~1200 usage hours in us-central during the spike window where we could've routed. Batch inference tolerance >5s so spots are OK.

elena: Latency-sensitive chat v2 traffic is APAC-first and must stay local. But offline embeddings & nightly reranks can be moved to us-west1 or us-central1 if cheaper. Need routing policy changes and canary rule.

priya: Proposed mitigation plan: 
- Revoke the accidental embedding sync (done)
- Move non-latency batch jobs to us-west1 (cheaper egress internal) + use preemptible for those fleets
- Trial a 6mo commitment for 40% baseline in ap-southeast1 to test actual savings vs forecast
- Add cost alert on network_egress per-project > $5k/day

alex: I'm +1. Quick config snippets:
```yaml
routing:
  - name: apac-latency
    match: tags: ["latency-sensitive"]
    preferred_regions: ["ap-southeast1"]
  - name: apac-batch
    match: tags: ["batch"]
    preferred_regions: ["us-west1", "us-central1"]
autoscale:
  fleet: batch-workers
  capacity_policy: spot-first
```

tyler: Finance: need a formal estimate before we sign commitment. Priya — can you paste the 6mo and 1yr delta in a short spreadsheet? Use committed capacity = 40% and 60% scenarios. I'll review and escalate to procurement.

priya: On it. I'll populate the sheet by EOD. Quick numbers from provider pricing page: a2-highgpu-1g on-demand $7.75/hr, 1yr commit ~ $6.05/hr. Spot ~ $2.10/hr. I'll model 40%/60% baseline for 6mo vs 1yr.

jordan: We should also model the hidden cost of cross-region egress if we decide to centralize some workloads. For APAC->US replication it adds ~0.75$/GB. Worth including in the sheet.

elena: Ops action: please add a temporary routing rule to prefer local model variants for latency-sensitive endpoints and fallback to cheaper regions only for batch operations. @sre-bot can we add a canary that shifts 5% batch traffic to us-west for 48h?

sre-bot: Canary scheduled: 5% shift of tag=batch -> us-west1 for 48h starting 1873456800. Will post metrics to #eng-metrics. :robot_face: 

alex: TL;DR decisions for now:
- revoke accidental sync (done)
- start 48h canary for batch region shift (sre-bot scheduled)
- priya to deliver cost model for 6mo/1yr commit options by EOD
- finance (tyler) will prepare procurement path if savings look real

tyler: Noted. Priya, cc me on the spreadsheet. If 1yr shows >18% savings net of expected extra egress, procurement can fast-track.

priya: shared sheet: https://internal.redwood/sheets/apac-commit-model-1873456789 — filling now, will ping when ready.

alex: thanks everyone. Once priya posts numbers we'll reconvene and decide on trial commitment. Also PR for routing rule pls so infra can version control it. :thumbsup: 

elena: I'll open the PR for routing policy after the canary completes and we validate perf.

jordan: Also adding a recurring check to detect accidental long-lived replication jobs (Nag for 7d).

alex: Perfect. Closing loop here — will follow up after the numbers & canary results. :lock:
